name: General Government
native: Generalgouvernement für die besetzten polnischen Gebiete
alt: General Government for the Occupied Polish Territories

predecessors.name: Second Polish Republic
predecessors.text: the part of pre-war Poland German forces held that was neither annexed to the Reich nor taken by the Soviets; the Reich 'had already annexed large parts of western pre-war Poland (8 October 1939)'…

successors.name: Poland (Polish People's Republic and Third Polish Republic)
successors.text: Poland, 'declared restored' on 22 July 1944; 'USSR captures Warsaw: 17 January 1945'; 'Disintegration: 19 January 1945'

ledger.x: 26 October 1939: the General Government is set up for the part of occupied Poland the Reich did not annex.
26 October 1939: Germany administers the General Government as occupied territory.
1 August 1941: the District of Galicia is added after Operation Barbarossa.

ledger.cpn: Poland (Polish People's Republic and Third Polish Republic)

ledger.x: 17-19 January 1945: the Red Army takes Warsaw and the General Government disintegrates.
January 1945: the remainder of the General Government passes to the restored Polish state.
ledger.cpn: Poland (Polish People's Republic and Third Polish Republic)

wars.name: Operation Barbarossa
wars.outcome: The Wehrmacht overran Soviet-held East Galicia in the first days of the invasion; on 1 August 1941 it became the District of Galicia of the General Government.

certainty.note: The border with the annexed Reich lands follows the October 1939 decrees and the border with the USSR the German-Soviet line of 28 September 1939 ('met again on September 28 to delineate a permanent border'); the pages give no survey, but…
The Soviet advance moved the front month by month; the pages date only 22 July 1944, 17 January 1945 and 19 January 1945.
